panels.visual: Zeno (young lean merchant, sunburnt, short dark beard) on the deck of a merchant ship from Cyprus loaded with tall jars of precious purple dye, sunny sea
panels.caption: About 312 BC, a merchant from Cyprus called Zeno sailed for Athens with a cargo of precious purple dye.

panels.visual: A storm smashing the ship on rocks near the coast, purple dye spilling into the waves, Zeno clinging to a plank
panels.caption: Near Athens his ship was wrecked. He lost everything.

panels.visual: Zeno, soaking wet and penniless, wandering into a small bookshop full of scroll racks in Athens; the bookseller looking up
panels.caption: Wet and penniless, he wandered into a bookshop.

panels.visual: Zeno sitting on a stool reading a scroll, eyes shining, a little thought bubble of barefoot Socrates asking questions in the Agora
panels.caption: He read about Socrates, who had died a hundred years before.

speech.speaker: Zeno
speech.text: Where can I find a man like this?

panels.visual: The bookseller pointing out of the shop door at a scruffy, cheerful philosopher with a staff and a ragged cloak, barefoot, walking past in the street
panels.caption: The bookseller pointed at a scruffy philosopher walking past: Crates.

panels.visual: Zeno blushing as he carries a big pot of lentil soup through a busy market; Crates smashing the pot with his staff and soup running down Zeno's legs, people laughing
panels.caption: Zeno became Crates's pupil. To cure his shyness, Crates made him carry soup through the market, then smashed the pot.

speech.speaker: Crates
speech.text: Why run? Nothing terrible has happened!

panels.visual: Years later: Zeno, now older, teaching a crowd of students in a long covered walkway with columns, its back wall covered in huge colourful paintings of a battle with soldiers and ships
panels.caption: Years later Zeno taught in the Painted Stoa, a long covered walkway on the edge of the Agora, painted with battle scenes.

panels.visual: Zeno's students proudly gathered between the columns of the Painted Stoa, waving, a banner-like caption
panels.caption: His followers were named after the place: Stoics.

panels.visual: Zeno calmly pointing up at a storm cloud he cannot stop, and then at his own calm heart
panels.caption: Stoics said: you can't control what happens to you. You CAN control how you respond.

panels.visual: A modern girl at a picnic as rain suddenly pours down; first she frowns, then she laughs and dances in the rain
panels.caption: Rain on your picnic? You can't stop the rain. Sulking or dancing: that part is up to you.

panels.visual: Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor (curly beard, laurel wreath, toga), writing in a notebook by lamplight in an army tent at night
panels.caption: Four hundred years later a Roman emperor, Marcus Aurelius, lived by these ideas. Find him at the Tower of the Winds.

panels.visual: Today: low excavated stone foundations of the Painted Stoa seen from behind a railing beside a modern street with cafes, a metro train passing, Glauka the owl perched on the railing pointing down
panels.caption: The Painted Stoa's ruins were dug up beside Adrianou Street. You can look down at them from the pavement.
